### Load and Set-Up Data 
```{bash}
# for Debaryomyces hansenii
# SEARCH: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/genome/GCF_000006445.2/
# Download the reference genome from refseq .fna file 
wget -nc -P data/https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/006/445/GCF_000006445.2_ASM644v2/GCF_000006445.2_ASM644v2_genomic.fna.gz

# Download the genome annotation file from refseq .ggf file 
wget -nc -P data/https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/006/445/GCF_000006445.2_ASM644v2/GCF_000006445.2_ASM644v2_genomic.gff.gz

# Download the reference proteome from refseq .faa file 
wget -nc -P data/https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/006/445/GCF_000006445.2_ASM644v2/GCF_000006445.2_ASM644v2_protein.faa.gz

# for Meyerozyma guilliermondii 
# SEARCH: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/datasets/genome/GCF_000149425.1/
# Download the reference genome from refseq .fna file 
wget -nc -P data/https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/149/425/GCF_000149425.1_ASM14942v1/GCF_000149425.1_ASM14942v1_genomic.fna.gz

# Download the genome annotation file from refseq .ggf file 
wget -nc -P data/https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/149/425/GCF_000149425.1_ASM14942v1/GCF_000149425.1_ASM14942v1_genomic.gff.gz

# Download the reference proteome from refseq .faa file 
wget -nc -P data/https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/genomes/all/GCF/000/149/425/GCF_000149425.1_ASM14942v1/GCF_000149425.1_ASM14942v1_protein.faa.gz
```

### Create Sequali Environment, if not already created. 
#### Set eval to FALSE to ensure code does not run during knit
```{bash, eval=FALSE}
conda create -n sequali-env python=3.11 -c conda-forge
conda activate sequali-env
conda install -c conda-forge -c bioconda sequali
```


### Run inital QC in Sequali Environment on d. Hansenii and m. Guilliermondii
Using Preliminary data 
```{bash, eval=FALSE}
conda activate sequali-env
sequali --outdir outputs_debaryomyces/dh_sequali_reports data_debaryomyces/debaryomycesHansenii.fastq
sequali --outdir outputs_meyerozyma/mg_sequali_reports data_meyerozyma/meyerozymaGuilliermondii.fastq
conda deactivate 
```

### Based on the above metric fliter the reads using filtlong
Use conda to install [filtlong](https://anaconda.org/channels/bioconda/packages/filtlong/overview) package. Allows filtering of long reads based on certain criteria. Ie. average Q score or size. 
```{bash, eval=FALSE}
conda install bioconda::filtlong
```

Run downloaded file to analyse using filtlong package.
based on the QC sequali html file: 
Filter the long read fastq to keep longest 75% of the sequences save results to outputs/ folder. 
```{bash, eval=FALSE}
filtlong --keep_percent 75 data_debaryomyces/debaryomycesHansenii.fastq | gzip > outputs_debaryomces/filtered_debaryomycesHansenii.fastq.gz
filtlong --keep_percent 75 data_meyerozyma/meyerozymaGuilliermondii.fastq | gzip > outputs_meyerozyma/filtered_meyerozymaGuilliermondii.fastq.gz
```

### Run Again QC in Sequali Environment to check filtered files
```{bash}
conda activate sequali-env
sequali --outdir outputs_debaryomyces/filtered_sequali_reports data_debaryomyces/filtered_debaryomycesHansenii.fastq
sequali --outdir outputs_meyerozyma/filtered_sequali_reports data_meyerozyma/filtered_meyerozymaGuilliermondii.fastq
conda deactivate 
```

## Assmebly 
### use Flye novo assembler

Create Flye environment if not already done
```{bash, eval=FALSE}
conda create -n flye-env python=3.10 -c conda-forge
conda activate flye-env
conda install flye=2.9.6 -c bioconda
```

Run 5 rounds of internal polishing
IDO ASK: Based on [Flye](https://github.com/mikolmogorov/Flye/blob/flye/docs/USAGE.md)
Why are you having us do 5 iterations/ runs? Reduce mapping errors by alignment to corrected assembly with subseqent iteration. how can you tell if you over polished? What biological background/ understanding is reqired? 
```{bash, eval=FALSE}
# Ensure the output directory exists
mkdir -p outputs_debaryomyces/flye_output
mkdir -p outputs_meyerozyma/flye_output

conda activate flye-env
# Run the Flye assembler, note the expected genome size
flye --nano-raw data_debaryomyces/filtered_debaryomycesHansenii.fastq --out-dir outputs_debaryomyces/flye_output --threads 8 --genome-size 12m --iterations 5
flye --nano-raw data_meyerozyma/filtered_meyerozymaGuilliermondii.fastq --out-dir outputs_meyerozyma/flye_output --threads 8 --genome-size 12m --iterations 5
conda deactivate 
```

## Polish draft assembly 
### Use medaka 
Create medaka environment, if not already done
```{bash, eval=FALSE}
conda create -n medaka_final -c conda-forge -c bioconda -c nanoporetech medaka python=3.10 -y
conda activate medaka_final
```

Run 2 rounds of medaka - Debaryomyces
```{bash}
# Activate your environment
conda activate medaka_final

# Ensure directories exist
mkdir -p outputs_debaryomyces/medaka_round1 outputs_debaryomyces/medaka_round2

# Round 1
medaka_consensus -i data_debaryomyces/filtered_debaryomycesHansenii.fastq -d outputs_debaryomyces/flye_output/assembly.fasta -o outputs_debaryomyces/medaka_round1 -t 8

# Round 2
medaka_consensus -i data_debaryomyces/filtered_debaryomycesHansenii.fastq -d outputs_debaryomyces/medaka_round1/consensus.fasta -o outputs_debaryomyces/medaka_round2 -t 8
```

Run 2 rounds of medaka - Meyerozyma
```{bash}
# Activate your environment
conda activate medaka_final

# Ensure directories exist
mkdir -p outputs_meyerozyma/medaka_round1 outputs_meyerozyma/medaka_round2

# Round 1
medaka_consensus -i data_meyerozyma/filtered_meyerozymaGuilliermondii.fastq -d outputs_meyerozyma/flye_output/assembly.fasta -o outputs_meyerozyma/medaka_round1 -t 8

# Round 2
medaka_consensus -i data_meyerozyma/filtered_meyerozymaGuilliermondii.fastq -d outputs_meyerozyma/medaka_round1/consensus.fasta -o outputs_meyerozyma/medaka_round2 -t 8
```

```{bash}
  ezlabgva/busco:v6.0.0_cv1 \
```


## Quast 

quast - Debaryomyces 
```{bash}
mkdir -p outputs_debaryomyces/quast_output

gunzip -k data_debaryomyces/*.gz

docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)":/data_debaryomyces -w /data_debaryomyces quay.io/biocontainers/quast:5.3.0--py313pl5321h5ca1c30_2 \
  quast.py outputs_debaryomyces/medaka_round2/consensus.fasta \
  -r data_debaryomyces/GCF_000006445.2_ASM644v2_genomic.fna \
  -g data_debaryomyces/GCF_000006445.2_ASM644v2_genomic.gff \
  -o outputs_debaryomyces/quast_output
```

quast - Meyerozyma
```{bash}
mkdir -p outputs_meyerozyma/quast_output

gunzip -k data_meyerozyma/*.gz

docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)":/data_meyerozyma -w /data_meyerozyma quay.io/biocontainers/quast:5.3.0--py313pl5321h5ca1c30_2 \
  quast.py outputs_meyerozyma/medaka_round2/consensus.fasta \
  -r data_meyerozyma/GCF_000149425.1_ASM14942v1_genomic.fna \
  -g data_meyerozyma/GCF_000149425.1_ASM14942v1_genomic.gff \
  -o outputs_meyerozyma/quast_output
```


## Evaluate the assembly
### Structural annotation - funannotate 
funannotate - Debaryomyces
```{bash, eval=FALSE}
mkdir -p outputs_debaryomyces/funannotate_out

gunzip -k data_debaryomyces/GCF_000006445.2_ASM644v2_protein.faa.gz

# Define reusable variables
IMAGE="nextgenusfs/funannotate:v1.8.15"
PLATFORM="--platform linux/amd64"
CPUS=8
INPUT="data_debaryomyces/assembly_polished.fasta"
SPECIES="Debaryomyces hansenii"   # e.g., "Pichia kluyveri" or "Hanseniaspora uvarum"
STRAIN="???"        # e.g., "RASPBERRY" or "NK1"

# Step 1: Clean redundant/short contigs ("genomic dust")
docker run -u $(id -u):$(id -g) --rm -v "$PWD":/data_debaryomyces -w /data_debaryomyces $PLATFORM $IMAGE \
  funannotate clean \
  -i $INPUT \
  -o data_debaryomyces/assembly_clean.fasta

# Step 2: Sort contigs by length and standardize header names (scaffold_1, etc.)
docker run -u $(id -u):$(id -g) --rm -v "$PWD":/data_debaryomyces -w /data_debaryomyces $PLATFORM $IMAGE \
  funannotate sort \
  -i data_debaryomyces/assembly_clean.fasta \
  -o dat_debaryomycesa/assembly_sorted.fasta

# Step 3: Soft-mask repetitive elements
docker run -u $(id -u):$(id -g) --rm -v "$PWD":/data_debaryomyces -w /data_debaryomyces $PLATFORM $IMAGE \
  funannotate mask \
  -i data_debaryomyces/assembly_sorted.fasta \
  -o data_debaryomyces/assembly_masked.fasta \
  --cpus $CPUS

# Step 4: Predict gene models using Saccharomycetes BUSCO models for training
docker run -u $(id -u):$(id -g) --rm -v "$PWD":/data_debaryomyces -w /data_debaryomyces $PLATFORM $IMAGE \
  funannotate predict \
  -i data_debaryomyces/assembly_masked.fasta \
  -o outputs_debaryomyces/funannotate_out \
  -s "$SPECIES" \
  --strain "$STRAIN" \
  --busco_db saccharomycetes \
  --augustus_species debaryomyces_hansenii
  --protein_evidence data/GCF_000006445.2_ASM644v2_protein.faa.gz
  --cpus $CPUS
```

funannotate - Meyerozyma
```{bash}
mkdir -p outputs_meyerozyma/funannotate_out

# Define reusable variables
IMAGE="nextgenusfs/funannotate:v1.8.15"
PLATFORM="--platform linux/amd64"
CPUS=8
INPUT="data_meyerozyma/assembly_polished.fasta"
SPECIES="Meyerozyma guilliermondii"   # e.g., "Pichia kluyveri" or "Hanseniaspora uvarum"
STRAIN="????"        # e.g., "RASPBERRY" or "NK1"

# Step 1: Clean redundant/short contigs ("genomic dust")
docker run -u $(id -u):$(id -g) --rm -v "$PWD":/data_meyerozyma -w /data_meyerozyma $PLATFORM $IMAGE \
  funannotate clean \
  -i $INPUT \
  -o data_meyerozyma/assembly_clean.fasta

# Step 2: Sort contigs by length and standardize header names (scaffold_1, etc.)
docker run -u $(id -u):$(id -g) --rm -v "$PWD":/data_meyerozyma -w /data_meyerozyma $PLATFORM $IMAGE \
  funannotate sort \
  -i data_meyerozyma/assembly_clean.fasta \
  -o data_meyerozyma/assembly_sorted.fasta

# Step 3: Soft-mask repetitive elements
docker run -u $(id -u):$(id -g) --rm -v "$PWD":/data_meyerozyma -w /data_meyerozyma $PLATFORM $IMAGE \
  funannotate mask \
  -i data_meyerozyma/assembly_sorted.fasta \
  -o data_meyerozyma/assembly_masked.fasta \
  --cpus $CPUS

# Step 4: Predict gene models using Saccharomycetes BUSCO models for training
docker run -u $(id -u):$(id -g) --rm -v "$PWD":/data_meyerozyma -w /data_meyerozyma $PLATFORM $IMAGE \
  funannotate predict \
  -i data_meyerozyma/assembly_masked.fasta \
  -o outputs_meyerozyma/funannotate_out \
  -s "$SPECIES" \
  --strain "$STRAIN" \
  --busco_db saccharomycetes \
  --augustus_species candida_albicans / pichia_stipitis\
  --protein_evidence data/GCF_000149425.1_ASM14942v1_protein.faa
  --cpus $CPUS
```


### eggNOG

```{bash}
# Create a dedicated Conda environment to install eggNOG-mapper and its fast sequence aligner (diamond):
conda create -n eggnog_env -c conda-forge -c bioconda python=3.10 eggnog-mapper

# run eggNOG-mapper
eval "$(conda shell.bash hook)"  # initialize conda 
conda activate eggnog_env

# USB to get eggnog_data on compute
EGGNOG_DB_PATH=/Users/hmangat02/Desktop/GenomicAnalysis/eggnog_db 

# Debaryomyces
emapper.py \
  -i outputs_debaryomyces/funannotate_out/predict_results/*.proteins.fa \
  --output isolate_functional \
  --output_dir outputs_debaryomyces/funannotate_out \
  --data_dir $EGGNOG_DB_PATH \
  --decorate_gff yes \
  --excel \
  -m diamond \
  --cpu 8
  
# Meyerozyma
emapper.py \
  -i outputs_meyerozyma/funannotate_out/predict_results/*.proteins.fa \
  --output isolate_functional \
  --output_dir outputs_meyerozyma/funannotate_out \
  --data_dir $EGGNOG_DB_PATH \
  --decorate_gff yes \
  --excel \
  -m diamond \
  --cpu 8
```
